hook: SCP-2701 is a single prison cell where a name and a release date written on a clipboard are enough to send someone away until that date. The premise is simple; the article's real subject is what that does to a human mind, and who first thought to use it. Expect descriptions of prisoner abuse, beatings and a suicide attempt.
whyItMatters: It is an anomaly about time and solitude rather than monsters: subjects are cut off from every sense while time stretches hundreds of times over, so even a short stay is long. The article pairs a clinical experiment with a confession, and the two interviews mirror each other, one subject begging not to be left alone again and one warden explaining how to break a living thing. The cadmium selenide on the door frame and the clipboard of release dates running as far as the year 33██ are left unexplained, keeping the cell's origin in shadow until the last exchange.
thingsToNotice:
The time dilation is the real horror: an estimated 300 to 400 times, so anything over two hours inside means weeks of total darkness and silence while fully awake. D-77391, picked because he had already done time in solitary, came out of a fifteen-minute event believing he had been gone for weeks, and he held together only because a doctor told him beforehand that he would come back; a suicide attempt 28 hours later ended in his termination, and that doctor was suspended for breaking protocol.

The addendum then explains where the names on the clipboard came from. Warden Samuel Decard, whose daughter Emily is named as the reason, meant the cell for one man, and when that man died in custody he turned it on the whole prison. Over three months and six days he starved, beat and dragged the inmates one by one into Cell 667, leaving suicides where they lay as a warning. Asked how he made the cell, he says he didn't: 'help' found him once he was willing to pay in hate and grief.
